summary: L-4 cab on Surprise Mountain in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, dated 1932 by most sources, staffed by the Mountaineers in 1943, removed or destroyed in the 1950s; a metal pole remains.

facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in the 1950s; SummitPost says a tall metallic pole is the only remnant

access.note: Summit reached on foot in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness; no source read says the site is closed

visit.trail_note: Hiking route from the Surprise Creek trailhead, about 13.6 miles round trip with about 4,400 feet of gain per a Mountaineers trip report; no source read describes a cab left to climb, and SummitPost reports only a tall metal pole as a remnant

events.note: Register, firelookout.com and SummitPost give 1932; Willhite's 1934 photo survey shows no structure and he guesses a cab went up about 1937
Mountaineers volunteers manned the lookout for the summer season, July 10 to August 31; no other staffing season appears in the sources read
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on May 22, 2012
Sources date the removal only to the 1950s; year 1950 stands for the decade. The register says removed; the others say destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register, firelookout.com and SummitPost give 1932. Willhite says the 1934 Osborne photo survey shows no structure and guesses a cab went up around 1937. The story reports both and does not choose.
The register says the cab was removed; SummitPost, firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed. All four date it to the 1950s.

sources.title: Surprise Mountain Lookout Site - Washington Fire Lookout

notes_for_editor: Build date is contested: 1932 in the register, firelookout.com and SummitPost, but Willhite's 1934 photo survey shows no structure and he guesses about 1937. The 2012 FFLOS registration date from the brief was confirmed on the register page (May 22, 2012). Destruction is dated only to the 1950s; events use 1950 as a decade placeholder. The Mountaineers trip report carries no date in the text read. Access is set to public because the summit is reached on foot in the wilderness; no closure was found. No new photos were added: the willhite page has captions but no image URLs were read. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 2014 photo caption does not name the lookout and sits among Evergreen Mountain Lookout captions, so the story hedges it. The telephone relay and the Mountaineers agreement are now quoted in full. The no-tower-to-climb point is no longer cited to SummitPost, which reports only a metal pole.
